newsitem.title: USA: NASD regulator revamps eligibilty arbitration rule.
newsitem.headline: NASD regulator revamps eligibilty arbitration rule.

text.p: The regulatory arm of the National Association of Securites Dealers (NASD) said Wednesday it revamped its "eligibility" rule that directs how investors claims are resolved through arbitration.

The newly revised rule retains only the six-year eligibility rule and assures investors of a single forum, Linda Feinberg, executive vice-president told reporters in a teleconference call. The new provision, subject to Securities and Exchange Commission approval, would allow investors to pursue the entirety of their claim, no matter when the injury was discovered, Feinberg said.
"The investor will now have a forum to bring its entire claim to, and this is particularly important with fradulent concealment claims," Feinberg said.

The original proposal, first approved in November 1996, eliminated the six-year eligibility rule, substituting a requirement that arbitrators must follow the applicable state and federal statutes of limitations.

The new rule is silent on the applicability of statutes of limitations and calls for the investor to first file the claim in arbitration and identify the dates of the transactions or other events in dispute.
The proposal provides that if all or some of the events complained of occurred more than six years before filing, and the member firms do not object, the entire claim will stay in arbitration.
NASD regulation officials will develop specific rule language to present to the NASD Regulation board and its parent NASD board in March.
The rule will then be resubmitted to the SEC for approval. During this time process, all interested parties will be able to file comments with the SEC.
